hypotheses.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite directed graph with $V=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $n\ge1$. Each vertex has at least one outgoing edge and belongs to exactly one of $V_{\mathrm{Max}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{Min}}$. The edge weights $w:E\to\mathbb Z$ are arbitrary signed binary integers.

For the operator in Equation [eq:operator] and arbitrary finite integer bounds $A\le u$, every subsolution $x$ and supersolution $y$ in $[A,u]$ satisfy $x_i\le y_i$ for all $i\in V$. There is a unique $h\in[A,u]$ that is both a subsolution and a supersolution. It is precisely the unique fixed point of $$T_{A,u}(z)=\min\{u,\max\{A,F(z)\}\}.$$ Consequently every such pair satisfies $x\le h\le y$.* *The following synchronous iteration finds $h$. Start with $p=A$; evaluate $q=T_{A,u}(p)$; return $p$ if $q=p$, and otherwise set $p=q$ and repeat. It uses at most $$1+\sum_{i\in V}(u_i-A_i)$$ evaluations of $T_{A,u}$, including the final stability test.

outputs.exact_statement:
A uniform deterministic algorithm returns exactly the set $$U=\bigl\{v\in V:\exists\text{ Max strategy }\sigma\ 
       \forall\text{ Min strategies }\tau,
       \ \mathop{\mathrm{MP}}_w(\pi_{v,\sigma,\tau})\ge0\bigr\}$$ for every game specified above. For an absolute constant $C>0$, the complete computation uses at most $$2^{C(\log_2(L+2))^2}$$ bit operations in a standard model polynomially equivalent to a uniform deterministic Turing machine. The bound includes preprocessing, exact arithmetic, recursion, and output of the entire set $U$.

For the operator in Equation [eq:operator] and arbitrary finite integer bounds $A\le u$, every subsolution $x$ and supersolution $y$ in $[A,u]$ satisfy $x_i\le y_i$ for all $i\in V$. There is a unique $h\in[A,u]$ that is both a subsolution and a supersolution. It is precisely the unique fixed point of $$T_{A,u}(z)=\min\{u,\max\{A,F(z)\}\}.$$ Consequently every such pair satisfies $x\le h\le y$.* *The following synchronous iteration finds $h$. Start with $p=A$; evaluate $q=T_{A,u}(p)$; return $p$ if $q=p$, and otherwise set $p=q$ and repeat. It uses at most $$1+\sum_{i\in V}(u_i-A_i)$$ evaluations of $T_{A,u}$, including the final stability test.

Let $h$ be the box solution in $[0,D_0]^V$. Then $$V_{\mathrm{lo}}=\{i:h_i\le nW\},\qquad
 V_{\mathrm{hi}}=\{i:h_i\ge D_0-nW\}$$ partition $V$. There is a positional Max strategy under which every play starting in $V_{\mathrm{hi}}$ has original mean payoff at least zero. There is a positional Min strategy under which every play starting in $V_{\mathrm{lo}}$ has original upper limiting average at most $-1/n$. Both assertions allow arbitrary history-dependent opposition.

A *Max witness* for $(A,D,a,b)$ is a subsolution $x\in[A,u]$ with support $S_x=\{i:x_i>A_i\}$ and $a(S_x)\le1$. It *claims* each $i$ with $x_i\ge u_i-P$. A *Min witness* is a supersolution $y\in[A,u]$ with support $S_y=\{i:y_i<u_i\}$ and $b(S_y)\le1$. It claims each $i$ with $y_i\le A_i+P$. A witness is *relevant* when it claims at least one index.

For every input in Equation [eq:recursive-input], the procedure $\ensuremath{\mathsf{Label}}(A,D,a,b)$ of Section 4 terminates and returns a vector in $\{+,-\}^V$. It assigns $+$ to every index claimed by any Max witness and $-$ to every index claimed by any Min witness.

Every recursive child is a valid input of the form Equation [eq:recursive-input], and its box is contained in its parent’s box. In a nonbase call the pivot satisfies $$\begin{aligned} c-M\le k\le c&\qquad\text{during the downward pass},\\ c-M\le k\le c+M&\qquad\text{during the upward pass}. \end{aligned}$$ If child calls terminate, each pass makes at most $1024n+1$ calls.

The procedure terminates on every input in Equation [eq:recursive-input]. Writing $D=2^d$, every child of a nonbase call has smaller rank $$R=d+B(\mu(a,b)).$$ The provisional child in Step 5 is the only child that preserves $B$. Every other child decreases $B$ by at least one.

For every relevant Max witness $x$, its peak $s_x(k)$ is constant throughout Step 3 and at most $D/2$. In particular, no Max witness claims an index in $I_-$. For every Min witness $y$ that has a claim outside $I_-$, $$b\bigl(\{i:g_i^y(k^{\downarrow})<q\}\bigr)>3/4.
 \label{eq:down-heavy}$$
Every parent Max witness with a claim outside $I_+$ remains a Max witness for $(A,D,\bar a,\bar b)$. Every parent Min witness with a claim outside $I_-$ remains a Min witness for that input.

A uniform deterministic algorithm returns the exact value $\operatorname{val}_w(v)$ as a reduced rational for every $v\in V$ and one positional strategy $\sigma^\star$ for Max and one positional strategy $\tau^\star$ for Min such that, simultaneously for every $v\in V$ and every pair of history-dependent strategies $\sigma,\tau$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{MP}}_w(\pi_{v,\sigma^\star,\tau})\ge\operatorname{val}_w(v),
 \qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{MP}}_w(\pi_{v,\sigma,\tau^\star})\le\operatorname{val}_w(v).$$ The complete computation takes $2^{O((\log_2(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations.

For the game model of Theorem 1, a uniform randomized algorithm returns all exact values and both globally optimal positional strategies specified in Corollary 14 with probability at least $7/8$ for the entire output. Its running time is $2^{O((\log_2(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations on every random tape.

Uniform deterministic algorithms have the following guarantees.* 1. *Given $v$ and a nonnegative binary integer $c$, decide whether $(v,c)$ is energy-winning. On a positive answer, return a positional Max policy satisfying Equation [eq:energy-objective] from that start and credit against every history-dependent Min strategy.* 2. *Given $v$, return the exact $c_{\min}(v)$, including the possible answer $\infty$. On a finite answer, return a positional Max policy winning from $v$ at credit $c_{\min}(v)$.* *The fixed-credit computation takes $2^{O((\log_2(L_c+2))^2)}$ bit operations, where $L_c$ is the full explicit input length including the start and credit. The minimum-credit computation takes $2^{O((\log_2(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations for the original game length $L$. Handling every vertex by separate per-start searches, including a separate policy for every finite answer, has the same form of total bit bound.* *Each policy may depend on the queried start and credit; it also wins from that same start at every larger credit.

coverage.checked_domain: Exhaustive 324 two-vertex complete directed games: all owners, weights in {-1,0,1}, box [0,2]^2; 24 single-vertex boundary cases; 2 additional cases with parallel edges, negative endpoints and collapsed coordinates.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exhaustive Cartesian enumeration of integer box vectors and exact rechecking of both subsolution and supersolution inequalities; candidate uses synchronous fmpz iteration.
